findings.text: Eight dispositions have stable labels: kill_process and kill_thread and trap and errno and user_notif and trace and log and allow. A read only availability value lists them in that order separated by spaces.

A log mapping entry holds a 32 bit selector followed by a pointer to a constant character label. A constant table pairs each selector for the eight dispositions with its label in availability order and ends with an entry whose label pointer is null.

A mask to text helper walks the mapping table in order and joins labels for set bits with a caller supplied separator into a bounded buffer, signalling failure if any copy would overflow and otherwise reporting success including the empty mask case. A single label lookup scans for an exact match and returns its selector. A text to mask helper clears its result, splits input on spaces, accumulates selectors for each token, and fails on any unknown token.

The logged mask read path renders the current global mask as space joined labels into a temporary buffer sized like the availability value, borrows the incoming control descriptor while substituting that buffer and its size, delegates to the generic string read path, and reports an invalid argument failure if rendering overflowed.

One string control handler accepts a table descriptor plus direction and user buffer triple, adjusts handling of a nonzero file position on the write direction, then delegates to a shared bounded string routine using the table data pointer and length limit. An alternate build of the same handler name is unavailable and reports a not implemented failure.

The shared string routine treats missing storage, zero limit or zero length as an empty successful transfer. On the write direction a strict mode resumes from the current file offset bounded by existing content length while a non strict mode restarts at the beginning, appends user bytes up to one less than the limit stopping at nul or newline, always nul terminates, and advances the position by the requested length. On the read direction it clamps content length to the limit, honors the file offset, copies at most the requested length, appends a newline when room remains, and updates length and position to the bytes produced.

Updating the logged mask requires administrative privilege and otherwise fails with a permission error. On success it captures user text through the generic string write path into a temporary buffer sized like the availability value, parses it to a mask, rejects unknown labels and any mask containing the allowance selector with an invalid argument error, and only then publishes the new global value.

Logging of mask changes does nothing when auditing is disabled. Otherwise it renders old and new masks as comma joined labels with distinct placeholders for no bits set, for a failed update, and for rendering overflow, then emits an audit record carrying both renderings and a success indicator derived from the update result.

Two controls are registered under a kernel secure computing directory at device initialization time. The first named actions_avail exposes the availability value read only with mode 0444 through the generic string handler. The second named actions_logged has mode 0644 with a custom handler that serves reads from the current mask and on writes captures the prior mask, performs the privileged update, and audits the transition including failures.

A per process cache inspection requires administrative capability in the initial user namespace against the open file and reports access failure otherwise. It then attempts to lock the target sighand and reports a missing process failure if that fails. When the target has no filter it unlocks and reports empty success. Otherwise it acquires an extra filter reference, unlocks, prints one line per syscall number for the native bitmap marking each number as allowed or filtered, repeats for a compat bitmap when that build option exists, releases the reference, and reports success.

A global pointer caches slab objects for queued signal descriptors. A global integer controls whether unexpectedly fatal signals produce diagnostics and is annotated for mostly read access. A translation unit marker requests creation of trace points for this file.

Marking the current thread as having pending work acquires its sighand spin lock with interrupt state saved, sets the thread pending flag, recomputes derived pending state, and releases the lock restoring interrupts.
The synchronous fault set comprises SIGSEGV and SIGBUS and SIGILL and SIGTRAP and SIGFPE and SIGSYS. Selection logic gives this subset priority when scanning the first pending word.

Signal selection computes pending minus blocked words, and if any bit remains in the first word restricts to the synchronous subset when any synchronous bit is present, returning the lowest numbered remaining signal there. Otherwise it scans later words in order for the first nonzero masked difference and returns its lowest set bit, with dedicated handling for one word and two word configurations and a loop for larger configurations, returning zero when nothing is deliverable.

A query for whether a signal lacks handling returns true for the global init task regardless of disposition. Otherwise it returns false when a custom handler is installed and when a fatal signal is already pending on a dying task, and it otherwise returns the negation of whether the task is under tracing, meaning traced tasks are treated as handled and untraced default or ignore dispositions as unhandled.

Dequeue selection followed by collection first chooses the lowest eligible signal then gathers its info. Collection locates queued entries matching that number, removes the first match, keeps the pending bit set when another entry for the same number remains and clears it otherwise, copies the stored info out, and either transfers preallocated timer entries with timer origin to a caller provided out parameter or frees other entries normally. When no entry is queued it synthesizes a user origin info record with zeroed identity fields and the chosen number.

The main dequeue path requires the sighand lock to be held by the caller. It first drains the thread private queue as a process scoped delivery and only when empty drains the shared queue as a thread group delivery, rearming an interval timer when the shared result is an alarm. It recomputes pending state, marks a job control stop dequeued flag when the result is a stop signal, and for timer origin entries attempts timer delivery which can consume the result and restart selection, finally returning the signal number or zero when none remains.

Synchronous only dequeue first tests whether any unblocked synchronous bit is present in the first pending word and returns zero immediately when not. Otherwise it scans the private queue in order for the first entry whose code indicates kernel origin beyond user and whose number belongs to the synchronous set, then applies same number last instance accounting to decide whether to clear the pending bit and recompute, removes and copies that entry, frees it, and returns its number, returning zero when no matching entry exists.

Fatal signal diagnostics fetch the current register state and executable reference, log the executable identity or command name with the signal number, and on 32 bit Intel builds without user mode architecture dump up to sixteen instruction bytes using a fault tolerant user read that stops on first failure. Register display runs with preemption disabled and reenabled around it, so failures in executable lookup fall back to a command only message and user read faults truncate rather than fail the report.
An early initialization helper parses an integer from its string argument into the global fatal diagnostics flag and unconditionally reports that the argument was consumed.

A handler selection enumeration provides three values named HANDLER_CURRENT and HANDLER_SIG_DFL and HANDLER_EXIT meaning use the currently installed disposition when reachable, always apply default disposition semantics, and expose the outcome only as the process exit code.

An assertion helper enters a read side critical section, loads the target sighand pointer under that protection, asserts that its lock is held when present, emits a one time warning when the pointer is absent, and exits the critical section.

Numeric process directed delivery resolves the identifier in the caller virtual pid namespace under read side protection and forwards the supplied signal and info. A credential predicate authorizes the operation when any pairing of caller real or effective user identity equals target real or saved user identity.

Asynchronous input output completion delivery validates the signal number, builds an info record with the supplied error number, an async input output origin code and an address payload carried in the pid field area, looks up the target task by pid object under read side protection, enforces credential and security policy checks, and when a nonzero signal remains attempts sighand locking to queue toward the thread group, mapping absent tasks and lock failures to a missing process result and permission or policy denials to their respective errors.

Process group and broadcast delivery first handles positive identifiers as single process sends and rejects the most negative integer as a missing process. Otherwise under task list read protection a value other than negative one targets either the named group or the caller group when zero, while negative one iterates all processes beyond identifier one excluding the caller thread group, counts attempts, remembers the last error that is not a permission denial, and returns that memory when any target existed, zero when all denials were permission based, or a missing process error when no target existed.

A family of helpers builds cleared fault info records carrying a signal number, code and user address plus specialty data, then either forces toward the current or named task or sends to a named task. Variants cover machine check bus errors restricted to async and sync access codes, bound range errors with address and lower and upper bounds, protection key violations with key index, performance trap reports with address and type and data plus an async flag derived from whether the trap is blocked, ptrace breakpoint traps carrying an error number, and trap number carrying faults.

Group directed sends acquire task list read protection around group resolution and delivery for both single group and broadcast forms. Pid directed forms instead use read side critical sections around identifier or pid object lookup, and the async completion form additionally requires successful sighand locking around queueing with unlock afterwards.

When selection finds a pending bit without a queued descriptor the info is synthesized rather than retrieved, so original sender identity and details are lost and replaced by generic user origin values. Preallocated timer descriptors bypass the normal free path on dequeue and depend on a later timer delivery step to drop their reference, so mishandling that out parameter leaks or double releases timer state.
